title: Verify: send your verification codes in your own email template
summary: Pin one of your email templates to a Verify custom email sender, and codes arrive in your own design, copy, and translations instead of Bird's built-in email.
body_markdown:
Verify can now send the one-time passcode in an email you designed. Build the email in[Email Templates](https://bird.com/docs/guides/email/templates) , publish it, and choose it as the body of your custom email sender. Your users get your layout, wording, and languages; Verify keeps checking codes, attempts, and expiry exactly as before. The guide[Your own verification email](https://bird.com/docs/guides/verify/email-template) walks through the setup, with the rules the template must meet and how to troubleshoot a refused save.


**Get started**


- [Your own verification email](https://bird.com/docs/guides/verify/email-template) : design the template, pin it to your sender, and check what your user receives
- [Senders and branding](https://bird.com/docs/guides/verify/senders) : the Bird-managed and custom senders for every Verify channel


## What's new


- **Your template, your domain** : pick a published transactional template under **Email** when you set up a custom sender on **Verify** › **Configure** › **Channels** , or for a single country in Destinations. Templates only send from an address on your own verified domain; the Bird Verify and Authifly senders keep Bird's built-in email.
- **Two variables** : show the passcode with` {{ code }}` and the minutes it stays valid at send time with` {{ expires_in_minutes }}` . Add up to 25 languages; the template's default language is the fallback.
- **Checked when you save and when you send** : every published language must show the code in the body, outside the subject and outside any link. A template that stops meeting the rules after a republish fails that email instead of sending a code-less message, and a pinned template cannot be deleted.
- **Safe in your logs** : the Verify log and message details keep the code masked, as they do for Bird's built-in email.


Ready to try it? Start with[Your own verification email](https://bird.com/docs/guides/verify/email-template) .
